input_description: Long read sequence data, with FASTQ as the default input type and optional FASTA, FAST5, sequencing summary, BAM, or RRMS inputs; optional reference and plasmid GenBank files; and optional parameters for sample naming, quality/length filtering, assembly, mapping, variant calling, annotation, and workflow execution.
output_description: Quality-control and filtering reports, assembled genome outputs, mapped read and assembly alignments, variant call files from Clair3 and FreeBayes plus a merged variant file, coverage tracks, annotation outputs from Bakta, SnpEff, and Liftoff, strain-level analysis outputs, provenance logs, and preprocessed reference files in GenBank, FASTA, and GFF3 formats.
enriched_description: Long Read WGS pipeline is a Common Workflow Language computational workflow for long-read whole-genome sequencing analysis. It performs reference preprocessing, LongReadSum quality control before and after Filtlong quality and length filtering, Flye assembly, Minimap2 mapping of filtered reads and assembly, Clair3 variant calling on reads, FreeBayes variant calling on assembly, merging of Clair3 and FreeBayes variants, optional Strainy strain-level analysis, optional Bakta annotation for genomes without a reference, SnpEff database building or downloading with functional annotation, and Liftoff annotation lift-over. Inputs include a long-read sequence file with default FASTQ and optional FASTA, FAST5, sequencing summary, BAM, or RRMS types; optional sample name; optional reference GenBank file; optional plasmid GenBank files merged with the reference; and parameters for filtering, assembly coverage, ploidy, Clair3 model, SnpEff database, annotation transfer, threads, and provenance. Outputs include LongReadSum and Filtlong report directories, Flye and QUAST output directories, mapped read and assembly BAM files with indexes, BED and coverage track files, indexed reference FASTA files, Clair3 VCF and FreeBayes variant files, a merged variant file, Bakta, Strainy, SnpEff, and Liftoff output directories, provenance logs, and preprocessed GenBank, FASTA, and GFF3 reference files. It supports long-read quality control, contamination and read filtering, genome assembly, read and assembly mapping, variant calling and merging, functional and genome annotation, annotation lift-over, strain-level analysis, and reference preprocessing in bioinformatics and genomics contexts, including plasmid-containing genome analyses when plasmid GenBank files are supplied.
